texts.preamble: Sohan Lal vs Suman Bala on 30 August, 2025 In The Court Of Ms. Sheetal Chaudhary Pradhan Additional Sessions Judge-02, South-East District Saket Courts, New Delhi Criminal Appeal No. 193/2024 Ps- Govind Puri U/Sec. 29 Pwdv Act In the matter of :- 1. Sohan Lal (Husband) S/o Late Sh. Inderraj Sharma R/o H. No. 519, Top Floor Neb Sarai, New Delhi -110048 Presently At :- 19, Kotla Mubarak Pur, New Delhi-110003. 2. Santosh Devi (Mother-in-law) W/o Late Sh. Inderraj Sharma 3. Manju (Sister-in-law) D/o Late Sh. Inderraj Sharma W/o Sh. Mukesh Both Residents Of :- H. No. 210, Leela Ram Market Masjid Moth, New Delhi-110049 4. Savita (Sister-in-law) D/o Late Sh. Inderraj Sharma W/o Sh. Amit Kaushik R/o 327, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi .... Appe Versus Suman Bala @ Sonu W/o Sh. Sohan Lal R/o H. No. 285, Pandit Mohalla Tughalkabad Village, New Delhi-110044 .... Resp Date of institution : 31.05.2024 Date of final arguments : 13.08.2025 Date of Decision : 30.08.2025 Decision : Appeal Dismis Order of Ld. Court Upheld. Ca No. 193/2024 Sohan Lal & Ors. Vs. texts.facts: Further, the compensation was also awarded to the tune of Rs.5,00,000/- to be paid by respondent no. 1, 2, 3 and 4 within three months from the date of the order. 2. Appellants herein were the respondents and respondent herein was the complainant before Ld. 3. As per record of Ld. Trial Court, the brief facts necessary for disposal of present appeal, are as follows :- CA No. 193/2024 Sohan Lal & Ors. Vs. Suman Bala Page no. 2 of 21 "That Respondent No.1/husband of complainant, Respondent No. 2 is the mother-in-law and Respondent No. 3 & 4 are the sisters-in laws of the complainant. The marriage of the complainant was solemnized with Respondent no.1 as per the Hindu rites and Ceremonies at Intezar Garden, Suraj Kund, Haryana on 03.12.2014 with great pomp and show in the presence of family members and friends. However, no child was born from the wedlock. Though Respondent No.3 is married but since the marriage of the Petitioner, she is residing at her parental home along with her children, by deserting her husband. It has been stated that Respondents and the complainant were residing in a shared household and and sharing the same kitchen, drawing room, bathroom and toilet at the shared household. It has been stated that just after the marriage, Respondents started harassing and taunting the complainant for bringing less dowry in marriage and after a few days of marriage Respondent No. 2 (mother-in-law) had taken all the gold and silver ornaments from the complainant which were gifted by her family members at the time of marriage on the pretext of keeping them in a safe locker. It has been stated that (sister-in-law) had apprised her that she has mortgaged all her gold ornaments with a gold smith for Rs.1,00,000/- without her permission and had lent the same to someone else on interest but now that person has run away with the money and the goldsmith is going to sell her gold ornaments and she had requested the complainant to arrange for Rs.1,00,000/- from somewhere and she had also CA No. 193/2024 Sohan Lal & Ors. Vs. Suman Bala Page no. 3 of 21 promised to the complainant that she would return the money within one month. It has been stated that thereafter the complainant had borrowed a sum of Rs. 1,00,000/- from her elder sister namely Pinki and given the same to the Respondent No.4. It has been stated that after one month, when the complainant had requested Respondent No.4 to return the said money, she got utter shock and surprise when Respondent No.4 stated that she had never borrowed a single penny from the complainant. It has been stated that the complainant was subjected to mental and physical cruelty by all the respondents despite meeting their demands and she was not provided with proper food and clothing and was slapped several times by the respondents. It has been stated that on 10.01.2018, the complainant called her Sohan Lal vs Suman Bala on 30 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45021970/ 2 brother Naveen and asked him either to take the complainant back with him or otherwise she would be killed by the Respondents for more dowry. Thereafter he came there to take the complainant back at her parental home and finally on 22.04.2018, a meeting of the respectable members of the society was called but due to adamant behavior of the Respondents, no compromise could take place. Hence, the the complainant was constrained to file the present petition." 4. Thereafter, vide order dated 29.03.2019, Notices were issued to respondents. Respondents entered their appearance through their counsel on 21.05.2019 and filed their Written Statement. Both the parties were directed to file their respective income affidavits in the present matter. Thereafter, during proceedings, due to non-appearance CA No. 193/2024 Sohan Lal & Ors. Vs. Suman Bala Page no. 4 of 21 of respondents, they were proceeded exparte by Ld. Trial Court vide its order dated 21.04.2022 and matter was fixed for complainant's evidence. 5. Thereafter, feeling aggrieved from the aforesaid order dated 21.04.2022, respondents have filed an application u/sec. 126(2) CrPC for setting aside the exparte order, which was dismissed vide order dated 15.02.2023 by Ld. Trial Court. Matter was then fixed for exparte complainant evidence. Subsequently, respondent appeared before Ld. Trial Court and offered for settlement with the complainant, however matter was not settled and on 10.05.2024, an application was moved on behalf of respondent no. 1to 4 for setting aside of exparte order dated 21.04.2022 and order dated 15.02.2023, however aforesaid application was also dismissed vide order dated 10.05.2024 by Ld. Trial Court and the impugned judgment was pronounced on the same day. 6. CW2- Naveen Kumar, tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.CW-2/A and CW-3- Mala Sharma, tendered her evidence by way of affidavit Ex.CW-3/A and they have relied upon the documents already exhibited by CW-1. Thereafter, complainant evidence was closed on 07.08.2023 and matter was fixed for final arguments. Thereafter, vide impugned judgment dated 10.05.2024, Respondent/ husband was directed to pay maintenance to complainant at the rate of Rs. 20,000/- per month from the date of filing of petition till complainant is legally entitled to receive maintenance and was also awarded compensation of Rs. 5,00,000/- to be paid by respondent no. 1, 2, 3 and 4 within three months from the date of the order.
texts.arguments: In addition, Ld. Counsel for appellants/ respondents has argued that Ld. Trial Court did not appreciate the material on record and that the complainant has left the matrimonial house by her own free will and has used the legal provisions only for extracting the money from the respondent/ husband. Lastly, he has argued that impugned order and judgment is vitiated by fatal infirmities and argued that impugned order and judgment dated 10.05.2024 passed by Ld. Trial Court, be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. He has relied upon the case law titled as (1) Rupali Gupta vs Rajat Gupta, 2016 (234) DLT 693, (2) Mamta Jaiswal vs. Rajesh Jaiswal, 2000 (3) MPLJ 100.; (3) NIharika Ghosh @ NIharika Kundu Vs. Shankar Ghosh 2023 DHC 6553 (4) Chetram Mali Vs. karishma Saini, 2023 DHC 8322 DB (5) Megha Khetrapal Vs. Rajat Kapoor 2025 DHC 1742 and (6) Rajnesh Vs. Neha (2021) 2 SCC 324. 13. Ld. Counsel for the complainant/ respondent herein has argued that impugned order passed by Ld. Trial Court, is legally correct and needs no interference. He has further argued that respondents did not appeared before the Ld. Trial Court intentionally and the grounds taken by the respondents in the present appeal are baseless and frivolous and present appeal is filed only just to delay the execution of the impugned judgment passed by Ld. Trial Court. Ld. Counsel has also relied upon the case laws titled as (1) Shailja & Anr. Vs. Khobanna (2018) 12 SCC 199 (2) Subhash Vs. Mamta @ Raksha, Mat Appl (FC) No. 195/2025 passed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi (3) Lalta Prasad Kushwaha Vs. Jayanti Kushwaha in FA No. 455/2018 passed by Hon'ble High Court of Allahabad (4) Kanpuriya Vs. State (2019) DLT 349 by Hon'ble High CA No. 193/2024 Sohan Lal & Ors. Vs. Suman Bala Page no. 9 of 21 Court of Delhi, (5) Babita Bisht Vs. Dharmender Singh Bisht 2010 (5) ADR 3234 by by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi and (6) Manish Jain Vs. Akansha Jain (2017) 15 SCC 801 by Hon'ble Apex Court. Where a woman is subjected to cruelty by her husband or her relatives for demand of dowry, it is an offence u/sec. 498A of the Indian Penal Code. It was therefore, proposed to enact a law keeping in view of the rights guaranteed under Article 14, 15 & 21 of the Constitution to provide for a remedy under the civil law which is intended to protect the woman from being victims of domestic violence and to prevalent the occurrence of the domestic violence in the society. Vs. Suman Bala Page no. 10 of 21 protect the woman from domestic violence in the society. If the choice is between two interpretations, the narrower of which would fail to achieve the manifest purpose of the legislation, we should avoid a Sohan Lal vs Suman Bala on 30 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45021970/ 6 construction which would reduce the legislation to futility. 16. The Act inter-alia provides for more effective protection or the right of woman guaranteed under the constitution who are victims of the domestic violence of any kind occurring within the shared household. According to the Act, any harm, injury to health, safety, life, limb or well being or any other act or threatening or coercion etc. by any adult member of the family, constitutes domestic violence. Further, the act also contemplates that any woman who is or has been in a domestic relationship, if she is subjected to any domestic violence can file a complaint u/sec. 12 of the PWDV Act. This Act also covers those woman who are or have been in relationship with the abuser where both parties have live together in a shared household and a relative by consanguinity, marriage or through a relationship in the nature of marriage or adoption. 18. It is borne out from the ordersheets of Ld. Trial Court that on several occasions, despite directions, the respondent/ husband was failed to file the affidavit of his income, assets and liabilities, as per the directions of Rajnesh Vs. Neha [(2021) 2 SCC 324]. Instead, the matter was repeatedly adjourned at the instance of the respondents on the ground that a settlement was under contemplation. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for respondents has taken the plea that respondent/ husband has the liabilities of widow mother and two sisters and therefore, the impugned judgment must be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. The Act provides for the rights of woman to secure housing and also to reside in her matrimonial home or a shared household whether or not she has any title or right in such home or household. In the case law titled as Chander Prakash Bodhraj v. Shila Rani Chander Prakash, AIR 1968 DELHI 174, wherein it has been held that ; "An able-bodied young man has to be presumed to be capable of earning sufficient money so as to be able reasonably to maintain his wife and child and he cannot be heard to say that he is not in a position to earn enough to be able to maintain them according to the family standard. It is for such able-bodies person to show to the Court cogent grounds for holding that he is unable to reasons beyond his control, to earn enough to discharge his legal obligation of maintaining his wife and child. When the husband does not disclose to the Court the exact amount of his income, the presumption will be easily permissible against him." 25. Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled as Rajnesh Vs Neha & Anr, Crl. Appeal No. 730/2020 (arising out of SLP (Crl) No. 9503/2018, dated 04.11.2020 has held as under :- Criteria for determining quantum of maintenance :- The objective of granting interim / permanent alimony is to ensure that the dependent spouse is not reduced to destitution or vagrancy on account of the failure of the marriage, and not as a punishment to the other spouse. There is no straitjacket formula for fixing the quantum of maintenance to be awarded. The factors which would weigh with the Court inter alia are the status of the parties; reasonable needs of the wife and dependent children; whether the applicant is educated and professionally qualified; whether the applicant has any independent source of income; whether the income is sufficient to enable her to maintain the same standard of living as she was accustomed to in her matrimonial home; whether the applicant was employed prior to her marriage; whether she was working during the CA No. 193/2024 Sohan Lal & Ors. Vs. Suman Bala Page no. 16 of 21 subsistence of the marriage; whether the wife was required to sacrifice her employment opportunities for nurturing the family, child rearing, and looking after adult members of the family; reasonable costs of litigation for a nonworking wife. Sohan Lal vs Suman Bala on 30 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45021970/ 9 26. Besides that, the court must take into consideration the status of the parties and the capacity of the spouse to pay for her or her child or his support, the financial capacity of the husband, his actual income, reasonable expenses for his own maintenance and dependent family members including his own child, whom he is obliged to maintain under the law, liabilities if any, would be required to be taken into consideration. The Court must have due regard to the standard of living of the husband, as well as the spiraling inflation rates and high costs of living. The plea of the husband that he does not possess any such source of income through which, he could maintain her wife, ipso facto does not absolve him of his moral duty to maintain his wife or his child if he is able bodied and has educational qualifications. Wife's education or earning capacity does not disqualify her from receiving maintenance or compensation under the DV Act. Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled as Rajnesh Vs Neha & Anr (Supra) has held as under :- CA No. 193/2024 Sohan Lal & Ors. Vs. Suman Bala Page no. 17 of 21 (c) Where wife is earning some income. The Courts have held that if the wife is earning, it cannot operate as a bar from being awarded maintenance by the husband. The Courts have provided guidance on this issue in the following judgments. 28. Further, in order to determine the quantum of maintenance payable to an applicant, the Court shall take into account the criteria enumerated in Part B - III of the judgment Rajnesh Vs Neha and Anr. (supra). The objective of granting interim / permanent alimony is to ensure that the dependent spouse is not reduced to destitution or vagrancy on account of the failure of the marriage, and not as a punishment to the other spouse. Further, it is a common and well-recognized tactic of the parties, particularly respondents in Domestic Violence Act (DV Act) cases, to conceal their true income or show it as lower than it is to avoid or reduce their financial obligations for maintenance.
